Motion planners

Source: R/planning.R
robot_planner.Rd

Configures a sampling-based planner in joint space. Validity of a configuration means: inside bounds (the joint limits by default) and, when a robot is given, free of collisions with environment and of self-collisions. A custom validity function function(q) returning TRUE for valid states can replace or refine this, which also allows planning for abstract point robots without a robot_model.

Usage

robot_planner(
  robot = NULL,
  algorithm = c("rrt_connect", "rrt", "rrt_star", "prm"),
  environment = NULL,
  validity = NULL,
  bounds = NULL,
  self = TRUE,
  margin = 0,
  step_size = 0.3,
  goal_bias = 0.05,
  max_iterations = 5000,
  resolution = 0.02,
  rewire_factor = 2,
  prm_nodes = 200,
  prm_neighbors = 8
)

Arguments

robot

Optional robot_model.

algorithm

Planner name.

environment

Optional robot_environment.

validity

Optional function of a configuration.

bounds

Matrix of c(lower, upper) rows; defaults to the robot's sampling bounds (limits, with unbounded joints sampled in \([-\pi, \pi]\) or \([-1, 1]\) m).

self

Check self-collision.

margin

Collision margin.

step_size

Maximum extension per tree step.

goal_bias

Probability of sampling the goal (RRT and RRT*).

max_iterations

Maximum number of samples.

resolution

Edge checking resolution.

rewire_factor

Scale \(\gamma\) of the RRT* radius \(\min(\gamma (\log n / n)^{1/d}, \text{step\_size})\).

prm_nodes, prm_neighbors

Roadmap size and connectivity.

Value

A robot_planner.

Details

Edges between states are straight lines in joint space, checked at samples no farther apart than resolution in any coordinate. This is a discrete check (see robot_check_path()). Distances are Euclidean in joint space; continuous joints are treated as bounded to \([-\pi, \pi]\) without wrap-around.

Algorithms:

  • "rrt": rapidly exploring random tree (LaValle, 1998) with goal bias.

  • "rrt_connect": bidirectional RRT with greedy connection (Kuffner and LaValle, 2000).

  • "rrt_star": RRT* (Karaman and Frazzoli, 2011) with rewiring in a shrinking radius. It is asymptotically optimal only as the number of samples grows without bound; with a finite max_iterations it returns the best path found so far.

  • "prm": probabilistic roadmap with prm_nodes samples and prm_neighbors nearest-neighbor connections, queried with Dijkstra's algorithm.

Examples

planner <- robot_planner(validity = function(q) sum((q - c(0.5, 0.5))^2) > 0.04,
                         bounds = rbind(c(0, 1), c(0, 1)),
                         algorithm = "rrt_connect")
plan <- robot_plan(planner, c(0.1, 0.1), c(0.9, 0.9), seed = 1)
plan$success
#> [1] TRUE
